title: How to Choose Wireless Earbuds: What Actually Matters
metaDescription: Phone compatibility, noise cancelling, fit and battery: a plain-English guide to choosing wireless earbuds.
lede: Spec sheets make every pair sound amazing. These are the factors that actually change how earbuds feel to use every day.

p: Apple, Samsung and Google earbuds all work best with their own phones, adding features such as automatic switching, easier pairing and better-supported audio. If you're firmly in one ecosystem, start with that brand's earbuds.
Earbuds that don't seal properly lose bass and noise cancelling. Look for multiple ear tip sizes and, for workouts, wings or bands that keep them in place.
Active noise cancelling (ANC) reduces steady background noise like engines and air conditioning. Transparency or ambient mode lets outside sound in so you can hear traffic and conversations.
These are worth a look before you buy:
list: Water and sweat resistance rating (IP rating) if you work out
Multipoint, to stay connected to a phone and a laptop at once
Battery life per charge and with the case
Codec support (for example LDAC or aptX) if you use an Android phone and care about audio quality

faqs.q: How long do wireless earbuds last?
faqs.a: Batteries slowly lose capacity, and many owners replace earbuds after two to four years of daily use. A warranty and replaceable tips help.
Not always. Flagships usually have better noise cancelling and call quality, but budget pairs can sound very good for music.
